sections.overview: Pseudolais pleurotaenia is a freshwater pangasiid catfish native to mainland Southeast Asia.
sections.identification: It has a slender body, a sharp abdominal keel and two pairs of short barbels; the tail is deeply forked.
sections.habitat: It occurs in major mainland river basins, including the Mekong, Chao Phraya, Meklong and Tapi, and uses both rapids and slower deep reaches.
sections.diet: Adults feed on terrestrial and aquatic insects, with smaller amounts of plant material reported.
sections.behavior: In parts of the Mekong in southern Laos, upstream movements have been recorded during the wet season; migration timing may vary among reaches.
sections.reproduction: Species-specific spawning information was not available in the sources reviewed.
sections.ecology: Its seasonal movements connect river reaches and tributaries; the cited migration observations refer to particular Mekong sites rather than the entire range.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports a Least Concern assessment from twenty eleven; that dated assessment should not be read as a current population survey.
